lessons.title: Lambdas with Receiver
lessons.content: A lambda with receiver (`T.() -> Unit`) lets the lambda body call methods on T directly, as if it were `this` - this is the mechanism behind `apply`, and behind every Compose/Gradle/Jetpack DSL you've used. It's what makes builder syntax read like configuration rather than function calls. Real scenario: Jetpack Compose's Modifier chain, or building a Retrofit-style request configuration block.

lessons.title: @DslMarker: Preventing Scope Leakage
lessons.content: In nested DSL builders, without @DslMarker an inner lambda can accidentally call methods on an outer receiver, producing confusing bugs. @DslMarker restricts implicit receiver access to only the nearest enclosing scope. Real scenario: a nested UI-building DSL (like Compose's own internals) where you don't want a `Column { Row { /* accidentally calls Column's methods here */ } }` situation.
